newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UNITED CITADEL STORMED BY TURKISH INVADERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNITED CITADEL STORMED BY TURKISH INVADERS.

text.p: Manchester United's 40-year unbeaten home record in European competition ended tamely on Wednesday as Turkish champions Fenerbahce trampled across one of British soccer's most hallowed grounds.

A deflected goal from Elvir Bolic with 12 minutes to go at Old Trafford earned the Turks a 1-0 victory. It gave them renewed hope of Champions' League qualification on a night which confirmed Porto as the first club to reach the quarter-finals.

The Portuguese side scored a 3-0 win over Norwegian opponents Rosenborg to maintain their 100 per cent winning start to group D after four matches, inspired by Serb winger Ljubimko Drulovic who scored one goal and set up the other two.

There were also important away wins for Atletico Madrid who beat Borussia Dortmund 2-1 and Ajax who defeated Rangers 1-0 in Glasgow, but neither could compare with Fenerbahce in terms of rewriting European soccer lore.

The first-half was a huge disappointment, the two sides managing just three shots on target between them as United struggled to regain their composure after conceding 11 goals in their previous two English league matches.

They looked more purposeful after the interval as they pushed forward in search of the victory which would have ensured their qualification alongside Juventus, but in the 78th minute it all went horribly wrong.
Bolic broke down the left, cut inside and fired a right-foot shot which ballooned off the shin of United defender David May and over goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel's head.
United manager Alec Ferguson, whose side could now struggle to qualify if they do not secure at least a point at home to Juventus next month, could not ignore the significance of the result.
"I hoped it wouldn't happen in my time, but it's happened," he said. "It's very, very disappointing.I thought we did enough to win the match."

Fenerbahce's players, in contrast, celebrated wildly after the final whistle and will be strong contenders for a place in the last eight if they win at home against bottom-of-the-table Rapid Vienna in three weeks.

Rapid felt the full force of Juventus on Wednesday as they were thrashed 5-0 with two goals apiece for Alen Boksic and Allessandro Del Piero. The Italian champions need just one point from their final two matches to ensure qualification.

AC Milan did their prospects some much-needed good with a 4-2 win over IFK Gothenburg, although they travel to Porto next month knowing a defeat will force them to sweat on the outcome of their final fixture against Rosenborg in December.
The group A table is now a three-way tussle between Ajax, Auxerre and Grasshopper Zurich after a solitary 39th minute goal from Dutchman Arnold Scholten condemned Rangers to a fourth straight defeat.

Ajax are currently level at the top on nine points with Grasshopper who built on Viorel Moldovan's two first-half goals, his first in the Champions' League, to score a crucial 3-1 win over Auxerre which could well prove significant in the final table.
Few will have enjoyed the night's results more than Atletico Madrid supporters, who saw their side lose 1-0 at home to Dortmund only two weeks ago.

The Spanish side reversed the outcome in Germany with first-half goals from Roberto and Yugoslav striker Milinko Pantic, although both sides should progress following Widzew Lodz's 2-0 home win over Steaua Bucharest.
The victory earned the Polish club their first points of the competition.
